subject: Response windows & pricing for SLA bundles
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Response windows & pricing for SLA bundles

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to follow up with a short summary of what we need to finalize: uptime guarantees for peak hours, clearly defined response windows for severity levels, and an example of how discounts would step as committed spend grows.

Key asks:
- 99.9% vs 99.95% uptime economics (monthly credits)
- Response windows for Sev-1/Sev-2/Sev-3 (hours and escalation coverage)
- Any onboarding / white-glove retainer options and pricing

Can you send a compact worksheet we can circulate internally? Ideally something our CFO/procurement can review this week.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
Brightline Health Systems

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Response windows & pricing for SLA bundles

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a short worksheet (SLA_Pricing_Table_v3.xlsx) that lays out three uptime bands, response windows, and a sample commit-based discount ladder. High level notes:

- Uptime bands: 99.5% / 99.9% / 99.95% with associated monthly credit slabs.
- Response windows (business hours / 24x7 add-on):
  * Sev-1: 1 hour initial response (24x7), 4-hour remediation SLA for critical throughput degradation
  * Sev-2: 4 hour initial response (business hours), 24-48 hour remediation target
  * Sev-3: Next-business-day response, standard triage
- White-glove onboarding: one-time retainer for runbook integration and warm-standby (quoted separately)

Jonas and Kim: added you in case procurement wants alternatives for blended uptime or a trial arrangement.

Next steps: if the worksheet looks reasonable, we can produce a single-page summary for CFO + a signed MOP (terms) to get PO-ready.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sales Director, Account Sales
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0176

Attachments: SLA_Pricing_Table_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Response windows & pricing for SLA bundles

Thanks — quick internal note and a recommended counter:

- For customers with predictable peak windows (like Brightline's 7–11am ET batch), propose a blended uptime option: 99.95% during peak hours, 99.9% off-peak; crediting calculated on a weighted basis. This reduces bill shock for the customer while preserving our capacity economics.
- Discount ladder suggestion: 0% (baseline), 7.5% at $250k ARR, 12% at $500k ARR, 18% at $1M ARR. Keep an opt-in extended onboarding retainer for large-scale migrations.
- Recommend a 30-day pilot with a capped credit exposure (e.g., 1% of monthly run-rate) instead of an open trial.

Kim: can you confirm whether the onboarding retainer should be one invoice or amortized over three months for accounting?

-Jonas
VP, Enterprise Sales Operations

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Response windows & pricing for SLA bundles

Hannah —

Thanks for the worksheet and Jonas' suggestions. A few responses from our side (circulated to CFO & cloud ops):

> For customers with predictable peak windows (like Brightline's 7–11am ET batch), propose a blended uptime option: 99.95% during peak hours, 99.9% off-peak; crediting calculated on a weighted basis.

This blended approach sounds useful — would want exact math in the worksheet (examples for our historical traffic mix).

On discounts: procurement would prefer a steeper initial discount to help with internal approvals. Example ask: 10% at $200k ARR, 16% at $450k, 22% at $900k. Is there flexibility on the first step?

Trial: a 30-day pilot with a cap on credits sounds reasonable so long as the cap is explicit. Also need to confirm data retention and audit log access for the pilot (SOC2/ISO evidence).

If you can send a revised worksheet with the blended uptime example and a doc we can route to legal (MOP/terms), we can aim to have a PO by end of next week.

Regards,
Sarah Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
Brightline Health Systems

4) Kimberly will follow up on amortization of onboarding retainer and provide the accounting treatment.

Can you confirm the target PO date? If end of next week still works, we'll prioritize the worksheet and MOP addendum today.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
